newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn, soy harvest still behind average pace.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn, soy harvest still behind average pace.

text.p: Farmers in Ohio made limited corn and soybean harvest progress during the week ended ended November 17, according to the latest crop weather report from the state's agricultural statistics service.
Soybean harvest was complete on 90 percent of the acreage, four points above the previous week, but most producers should be finished at this time of year, the report said.
Corn harvesting was 61 percent complete, up from 51 the previous week. That figure compared with the five-year average of 81 percent.
More than 80 percent of the corn crop had been harvested in the northwest, while eastern and southern areas have more than half remaining.
Wheat had emerged on 89 percent of the acreage, compared with 78 the previous week, 98 last year and the average of 95 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated mostly adequate to suplust as of November 15, and there were four days suitable for fieldwork, according to the report.
